stem:
Lalit writes numbers with Roman landmarks: I $=1$, V $=5$, X $=10$, L $=50$. He wants to represent $48$.

Which plan follows landmark decomposition?

options.text: Answer "Roman numerals", naming the system instead of building $48$ from landmarks.
String any mix of I, V, X, L without taking as many of the largest useful landmark as possible first.
Take one XL for $40$ (the largest useful landmark not past $48$), then VIII for the remaining $8$, writing XLVIII.
Copy the Hindu–Arabic digits $4$ and $8$ as shapes, and treat those drawn shapes as the Roman form.

teacher.key_rationale: Landmark systems take as many copies as possible of the largest useful landmark, then smaller ones for the remainder: 48 = XL + VIII = XLVIII.
